title: IBM unveils first Illinois quantum computer in Chicago
summary: Housed at UChicago's Hyde Park Labs, the IBM Quantum System Two will anchor Illinois' National Quantum Algorithm Center before moving to IQMP.
bullets:
- **IBM** International Business Machines Corporation unveiled an IBM Quantum System Two at the **University of Chicago**'s Hyde Park Labs on Friday and calls it its most advanced system.
- The machine runs IBM's **Nighthawk r2** processor, which has 120 qubits according to IBM. Cloud customers can already use it under the name "ibm_chicago".
- It will later move to the **IQMP** campus on Chicago's South Side, where Illinois has committed $500 million, the Chicago Tribune reported.

sections.heading: IBM unveils first Illinois quantum computer in Chicago
sections.body: IBM unveiled its first quantum computer in Illinois on Friday, November 6, an IBM Quantum System Two at the University of Chicago's Hyde Park Labs. The company describes it as its most advanced system available. IBM unveiled it together with the University of Chicago, the State of Illinois and the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP), and the machine runs on IBM Quantum Nighthawk, the most powerful quantum chip IBM has built, according to IBM. The system will anchor the state's National Quantum Algorithm Center. It will later move to the IQMP campus going up on the former U.S. Steel site on Chicago's South Side, the Chicago Tribune reported.

sections.heading: A public-facing machine
sections.body:
The computer uses the Nighthawk r2 processor. It sits at street level behind floor-to-ceiling windows on 53rd Street, IBM's quantum blog said. IQMP CEO Harley Johnson called it "probably the most publicly visible quantum computer in the world." IBM lists Nighthawk r2 with 120 programmable qubits and up to 25 times the speed of the previous generation, according to its hardware page. Cloud customers on Premium, Flex and Pay-As-You-Go plans can already use the new processor under the name "ibm_chicago," IBM's service changelog shows.

"I want the next generation of breakthroughs to happen in Illinois and the jobs and opportunity that come with them to benefit the people of Illinois," Governor JB Pritzker said in the release. IBM CEO Arvind Krishna said the system "can deliver scientifically useful results to organizations across the state of Illinois and beyond."

sections.heading: Building a quantum hub
sections.body:
Pritzker set up the algorithm center in 2024, with IBM as a leading member. Its Grand Challenge participants include Deloitte and AbbVie, which are working with IBM and Northwestern University on molecular simulation for drug discovery, IBM said. Separately, EPRI and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign are studying quantum optimization for power grids.

System Two machines already run in New York, Japan and Spain, the Tribune noted. The state has committed $500 million to the quantum park, including $200 million for a shared cryogenic plant. PsiQuantum is also building at the site. In April, IBM announced its FutureNow Chicago center at the park and said it would create 750 jobs. The center will be an anchor tenant in the Quantum Works building, which is expected to be finished by 2028.

sections.heading: Research momentum
sections.body:
Earlier this year, a team from the University of Chicago and IBM showed quantum advantage on a structured computing task. The experiment used 70 logical qubits and finished in about 15 minutes, IBM's blog said. UChicago Vice President of Research Nadya Mason said, "For our graduate students, having access to a quantum computer is incredible."

IBM will hold its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago from November 11 to 13, according to its events page.

title: Great Pacific Garbage Patch changing color of ocean
summary: Bergen researchers say satellite data from 2002 to 2022 shows North Pacific brightening, though direct sampling is needed to confirm plastics' role.
bullets:
- **University of Bergen** scientists reported Thursday that waters near the **Great Pacific Garbage Patch** have turned more cyan over two decades.
- Three satellite records showed blue and green brightening, and models found adding microplastics made the cyan pattern over four times more likely.
- Researcher **Shea Cheatham** told CNN that on-site measurements are needed, but confirmation could let satellites track microplastics from space.

sections.heading: Microplastics may be turning ocean near Great Pacific Garbage Patch cyan
sections.body:
For two decades, a stretch of the North Pacific between Hawaii and California has been getting brighter in blue and green light. Researchers in Norway say a buildup of tiny plastic particles may be part of the reason. A study published Thursday, Nov. 5, in Communications Earth & Environment looked at three satellite records from 2002 to 2022. All three showed statistically significant brightening in both bands in and near the Great Pacific Garbage Patch, which together produced a cyan tint.

The authors are Shea Cheatham, Daniel Koestner and Børge Hamre, all at the University of Bergen. They say the satellite pattern matches the optical signature that suspended microplastics would produce. They also stress that the satellite data by itself does not prove plastic is the cause.

sections.heading: A signal in the satellite data
sections.body:
The team used three ocean-color products: MODIS imagery from NASA's Aqua satellite, Europe's Ocean Colour Climate Change Initiative data and Copernicus-GlobColour. The cyan areas were clearest between 30 and 40 degrees north, roughly where microplastics are expected to collect. In some areas, blue wavelengths brightened by about 10% and green by 2% to 4% over the 20 years.

"What's interesting about the optical signature of microplastics is that they generally do not absorb much light at all across the visible spectrum, and are strong scatterers," Cheatham told ScienceAlert.

The researchers also ran simulations of how light reflects off seawater. When only natural factors were varied, the cyan pattern showed up in 3% of the brightening cases. When microplastics were added, that share rose to 13%, more than four times as often. In the models, about 5 milligrams of microplastics per cubic meter of water was enough to produce a change satellites could detect.

sections.heading: Caveats and next steps
sections.body:
The three satellite products did not agree everywhere. The authors point to known drift in the MODIS sensor and to differences in how the products correct for the atmosphere. Natural changes can also produce the cyan pattern, but only with large drops in suspended particles and dissolved organic matter and a shift toward smaller phytoplankton. The authors do not rule out disruption of the ecosystem as another cause or a contributing one. Very small microplastics under 300 micrometers have never been measured directly in the patch's upper waters.

Cheatham told CNN that more work is needed to prove the color "is directly and exclusively caused by plastics." The next step is to take measurements at the patch itself, which is difficult and expensive. If the link is confirmed, the authors say satellite color readings could become a way to track microplastic buildup from space.

"We're still one step away from proving definitively that microplastics are causing the shift in color that we're seeing," Cheatham told Scientific American. "We just have to get in there to verify."

title: Bluetooth 7 Speeds Are Set to Quadruple in 2027, Especially for Audio - CNET
summary: The Bluetooth Group has announced a new standard. Here's how it works and when you can expect to benefit from it.
text:
The Bluetooth Group has announced a new standard. Here's how it works and when you can expect to benefit from it.

Bluetooth is about to get an upgrade. The Good Brigade/Getty Wireless tech is about to get a whole lot snappier. On Thursday, the Bluetooth Special Interest Group, the trade association that oversees Bluetooth, officially unveiled Bluetooth High Data Throughput, a flagship upgrade set to arrive as part of the Bluetooth Core 7.0 standard. The revision supercharges Bluetooth Low Energy by pushing maximum bit rates to 7.5Mbps, effectively quadrupling the throughput of the existing LE 2M technology. Compatible devices are slated to hit store shelves starting in 2027.

That’s good news for phone users , tablet havers , laptop groupies, smart speaker stans and more. Bluetooth is still the most popular medium-to-short-range wireless standard for connecting devices. But this is a big rollout, and the changes will start with premium wireless, such as earbuds, with other applications following.

Those other applications could include spatial computing, exchanging AI-related info with local devices, connecting to health wearables and a host of smart home applications, like playing Spotify through an Amazon Echo Studio or dimming a smart bulb .

title: NASA, ESA release Hubble view of ancient star cluster M30
summary: The image blends data from three Hubble programs, showing a cluster astronomers suspect the Milky Way captured long ago.
bullets:
- **ESA** released the Hubble image of globular cluster **Messier 30** on Nov. 5 as its Picture of the Month, and **NASA** published it Nov. 6.
- The image combines ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared data from three Hubble programs, one of which tracked how the cluster's star groups moved over 15 years.
- M30 orbits opposite to the **Milky Way**'s spin, which researchers say suggests the galaxy may have captured it long ago.

sections.heading: Hubble image of star cluster Messier 30 released
sections.body:
A new image from the NASA/ESA Hubble Space Telescope shows the globular cluster Messier 30 (M30), a dense, ancient group of stars that astronomers say can help explain how the Milky Way developed. ESA released the image on Nov. 5, 2026 as its ESA/Hubble Picture of the Month, and NASA published it on Nov. 6. The cluster, also known as NGC 7099, sits about 27,500 light-years away in the constellation Capricornus.

The cluster is named for French astronomer Charles Messier, who listed it among the fuzzy objects that early telescope users could mistake for comets.

sections.heading: Three programs, one picture
sections.body:
The new view combines data from three Hubble observing programs and covers ultraviolet, visible and near-infrared light. The first, led by Ata Sarajedini, used the Advanced Camera for Surveys to study dozens of Milky Way globular clusters in red and near-infrared light, picking up stars as small as 20% of the Sun's mass. A second program, led by Giampaolo Piotto, used Wide Field Camera 3 with filters for bluer light. That data helped researchers study "blue straggler" stars and the multiple stellar populations that can live within one cluster. A third program, led by Mattia Libralato, tracked how those populations moved over the 15 years since Hubble first observed them.

An earlier Hubble image of M30, made only from Advanced Camera for Surveys data, showed several hundred thousand stars in a cluster about 90 light-years across that formed 13 billion years ago.

sections.heading: Clues to galactic history
sections.body:
Globular clusters are roughly spherical groups of tens of thousands to millions of stars. They usually orbit in a galaxy's halo, and the Milky Way has at least 150 of them, according to ESA/Hubble. Astronomers estimate their ages at 11.5 billion to 13.5 billion years, so some are nearly as old as the universe. Clusters that formed inside the galaxy can act as time capsules that preserve its early chemistry.

These clusters have shaped what astronomers know about the galaxy for more than a century. Harlow Shapley used variable stars in globular clusters to show that the Sun is not at the center of the Milky Way. His distance measurements were wrong, though, and led him to think the galaxy was about twice its actual size.

M30 may not have formed in the Milky Way at all. Researchers have found that it and many other globular clusters orbit in the opposite direction to the galaxy's spin. That suggests the Milky Way may have captured them long ago.

title: White House postpones tech panel with Huang, Zuckerberg
summary: The delay came a day after a tech stock rout driven by fears a Democratic Congress will slow AI data center growth.
bullets:
- The **Trump administration** postponed Friday's White House tech panel meeting with **Nvidia**'s Jensen Huang and **Meta**'s Mark Zuckerberg, an Energy Department spokesperson told Reuters.
- A **Federal Register** notice rescheduled the virtual meeting of the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, which had been set for Nov. 6.
- The delay followed Thursday's sharp AI stock sell-off after Democrats won Congress, sparking fears of regulation slowing data center buildout, per CNBC Versant Media Group, Inc..

sections.heading: Trump administration postpones White House tech panel meeting with Huang and Zuckerberg
sections.body:
The Trump administration postponed a Friday, November 6, meeting of the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology (PCAST). The White House panel's members include Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, Reuters reported, citing an Energy Department spokesperson. The White House did not immediately say why.

The delay came one day after a steep drop in technology stocks. Investors are worried that a Congress controlled by Democrats will slow artificial intelligence development, and that heavy AI spending will not pay off, according to an updated Reuters report.

sections.heading: Who sits on the council
sections.body: PCAST is an outside panel that advises the White House on science and technology policy. Its members also include AMD CEO Lisa Su, Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison and Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Marc Andreessen. Venture capitalist David Sacks and White House tech adviser Michael Kratsios co-chair the panel. The meeting announcement said the council would advise Trump's new "Super Intelligence Task Force," a group of cabinet officials, appointees and White House staff. Super intelligence is the president's preferred term for AI.

sections.heading: Confusion over a new date
sections.body:
The Energy Department, which handles the council's administration, had planned a one-hour virtual meeting from noon to 1 p.m. EST on November 6, according to an October 22 Federal Register notice. A second notice published November 6 moved the meeting to Friday, November 13, at the same time. The agenda listed a chair update, charges to the board and public comments.

Reuters reported that the department's meeting website briefly showed November 13 as the new date. The agency then sent an email taking that date back, so it is unclear when the panel will meet.

sections.heading: Market turmoil after midterms
sections.body:
The postponement came amid a sharp market sell-off. On Thursday, November 5, the Nasdaq Composite posted its biggest one-day drop in 19 months and entered correction territory. Chipmakers fell the most on fears of tighter AI regulation after Democrats won control of Congress. Nvidia lost 9.3% and AMD fell 17.3% that day, CNBC reported, although tech shares showed signs of recovering by Friday morning.

During the campaign, many voters pushed back against new data centers over water and energy use, NPR reported. Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has pledged to halt new data center construction in the state. "There is some concern regarding AI regulation, and fears that there could be far more regulations coming to AI technology," David Busch, chief investment officer of Trajan Wealth, told NPR.

title: TSMC weighs making memory chips for Nvidia, report says
summary: The world's largest contract chipmaker, which mainly makes logic chips, is planning 3D DRAM production, The Information reported, lifting its shares.
bullets:
- **TSMC** Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited has started planning to make stacked 3D DRAM memory at the request of **Nvidia** NVIDIA Corporation, its biggest customer, according to The Information.
- AI demand has outpaced memory supply and driven up hardware costs; TSMC is deciding whether to build new plants or convert an existing one.
- TSMC's U.S.-listed shares rose sharply Friday, but the move would put it in competition with **Samsung** Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. and partner **SK Hynix** SK hynix Inc..

sections.heading: TSMC weighs making advanced 3D DRAM memory chips for Nvidia
sections.body: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is considering a move into advanced memory chip production, The Information reported on Friday, citing two people with direct knowledge of the matter. The world's largest contract chipmaker has makes logic chips almost exclusively, so memory production would be a strategic shift. It would also give TSMC a larger share of the money flowing into AI hardware. According to Reuters, the company recently started planning to make a type of memory called 3D DRAM at the request of Nvidia, its biggest customer. TSMC and Nvidia did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

sections.heading: Fabs, leadership and market reaction
sections.body:
TSMC is deciding whether to build dedicated fabs or buy an existing plant and convert it, Investing.com reported via Yahoo Finance. Micron Technology took the second route in March, when it agreed to buy a Taiwan facility from Powerchip Semiconductor Manufacturing for $1.8 billion and retrofit it for high-end memory.

Vice president Hsu Kuo-chin is leading the effort. He runs TSMC's advanced packaging operations and previously managed Micron's regional business, according to The Economic Times.

TSMC's U.S.-listed American depositary receipts rose sharply in early trading on Friday after the report. The gain came as chip stocks recovered from a sell-off on Thursday.

sections.heading: Memory shortage drives the push
sections.body: Memory supply has not kept up with AI demand, and the shortage has pushed hardware costs higher. Nvidia and Apple are among the buyers looking for other sources of supply, and Apple raised prices across its hardware lineup earlier this year after its memory costs climbed. Conventional DRAM lays memory cells out in a single horizontal layer, while 3D DRAM stacks them vertically to increase capacity.

sections.heading: Risks and rivals
sections.body:
A move into memory would put TSMC in direct competition with Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron, which have long dominated the market. TSMC holds patents on vertical DRAM, but The Information reported that moving from development to mass production could take years. Memory makers also go through repeated cycles of shortage and oversupply, which can swing prices and margins.

The plan could also complicate TSMC's partnership with SK Hynix. In April 2024, the two companies agreed to collaborate on HBM4, with SK Hynix planning to use TSMC's logic process to make the memory's base die. That arrangement could now put TSMC in the position of supplying a company it may soon compete against.

title: PSA: Want To Learn Link's Ocarina Tunes? Nintendo's Got The Sheet Music For All Of Them - Nintendo Life
text:
Whether you have been playing Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, watching the trailers, or just been in the ether of its release, you almost certainly have an ocarina melody or two stuck in your head right now. For those who want to channel their earworm into a lesson, Nintendo has shared the sheet music for each of Link's in-game tunes, so you can stop whistling Zelda's Lullaby and learn to play it instead.

Nintendo previously announced that it'd share music how-tos via the Zelda Notes app, so you could work out how to play the tunes on any real-world ocarinas you may have accumulated over the years. But look, all of them are also available on the game's Japanese website , so you don't need to worry about unlocking them in-game before you start learning!

Alongside the sheet music, the website also includes specific ocarina finger placement to follow along with on the titular instrument.

Oh yes, and just in case these 12 tunes aren't already ingrained in your heads, the site (and app) also features a handy 'Play' button, so you can listen to how each of them is meant to sound before taking a stab at 'em yourself.

Of course, you might be waiting to learn any of these until you have one of the official tie-in ocarinas in your hands. Pre-orders for HORI's electric model went live back in September, and we are now seeing orders slowly trickle out for the playable version in select regional Nintendo stores.

title: Activists storm Microsoft data center site in Amsterdam
summary: The breach on Friday started two days of protests by the Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition, which wants large-scale construction halted.
bullets:
- More than 100 activists entered **Microsoft's** Microsoft Corporation Amsterdam construction site on Friday, climbing cranes and dancing while police stood by, according to **Reuters**.
- The coalition's map shows actions at 85 locations, including a Dublin march, a Warsaw rally and a Saturday protest at a Danish Microsoft site.
- Developer **Pure Data Centres** asked protesters to leave and talk with the company, while Microsoft said it does not condone unlawful actions.

sections.heading: Stop Dirty Data Centres coalition launches two days of protests across Europe
sections.body: Protesters broke into the construction site of a Microsoft AI data centre in Amsterdam on Friday, November 6. It was the first of two days of rallies against the rapid build-out of AI computing infrastructure, Reuters reported. The "Stop Dirty Data Centres" coalition says activist groups have announced actions in 16 countries on Friday and Saturday. The coalition brings environmental groups and digital rights campaigns together behind a call to pause large-scale construction.

sections.heading: Breach in Amsterdam
sections.body:
A Reuters witness counted more than 100 activists. They marched arm in arm before entering the site, then climbed cranes, hung balloons and danced while police stood by. Some carried placards reading "Screw your datacentre". Crowd estimates varied. Ritzau, writing in The Copenhagen Post, put the number at about 200. A spokesperson for organiser Geef Tegengas told local broadcaster AT5 it was closer to 500, according to Capacity. Capacity also reported that the mayor had banned the demonstration and that riot police made several arrests at the Sloterdijk site.

Denmark's Green Youth Movement said in a press release that Danish activists took part, alongside protesters from Germany, France, Portugal and Spain.

The site belongs to Pure Data Centres, which plans to invest more than $1 billion and is backed by Oaktree, a firm owned by Brookfield. "We respectfully ask those on site to leave safely and engage with us in dialogue about the development and any concerns they may have," the company said. Microsoft said it respected people's right to express their views peacefully but did not condone unlawful actions.

sections.heading: More actions this weekend
sections.body: Other planned protests include a march in Dublin, a rally outside the Polish parliament in Warsaw and a demonstration against a different Microsoft data centre in Denmark. The Danish protest is set for Saturday, November 7. A map on the coalition's website shows actions at 85 locations. Some earlier reports said more than 100 groups from 15 countries would take part, with Greenpeace and Foxglove among them.

sections.heading: Calls for a moratorium
sections.body:
Campaigners say data centres strain electricity and water supplies, compete with housing for scarce resources and threaten climate goals. The coalition says it is not against progress and is not seeking to close existing facilities. It wants major construction halted until governments set clearer rules.

Campaign coordinator Owen Espley linked the protests to this week's US midterms, saying the results "reflect shared concerns on both sides of the Atlantic". EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen called AI "a super important technology" for Europe. She added that citizens must be able to trust "their energy bills are not skyrocketing" because of data centres.

title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small, weights later
summary: Mira Murati's lab offers the 594B-parameter model only through Tinker for now and says open weights will follow external safety testing.
bullets:
- **Thinking Machines Lab** released **Inkling 2 Small** on Thursday. It is a mixture-of-experts model with 17 billion active parameters, available only through the lab's **Tinker** platform for now.
- It scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, up from its predecessor's 13. That puts it roughly level with Google's Alphabet Inc. **Gemini 3.8 Flash**, The Decoder reports.
- The lab says it will release the weights under an Apache 2.0 license after safety testing. It is also reportedly close to closing a $5 billion funding round.

sections.heading: Thinking Machines launches Inkling 2 Small with weights closed at first
sections.body:
Thinking Machines Lab, the startup founded by former OpenAI chief technology officer Mira Murati, released Inkling 2 Small on Thursday, November 5. The model is its second generation and its most capable so far. For now it is available only through the company's Tinker platform, and its weights are closed. The lab said it plans to release the full weights under an Apache 2.0 license next week, after external safety testing and red-teaming are finished.

The model is a mixture-of-experts system with 594 billion total parameters, of which 17 billion are active at a time. It accepts text and image inputs, lets users adjust how much reasoning effort it applies, and scores 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, according to the company. Its predecessor, Inkling Small, scored 13 on the same index, and the new score puts it roughly level with Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash, The Decoder reported. The company calls it the strongest Western open-weight model, although that claim depends on the weights actually shipping.

sections.heading: Gains in agentic work, at a higher cost
sections.body:
The biggest improvements are in agentic tasks. Its score on AutomationBench-AA rose from 5% to 46%, and its FrontierCode 2.0 score went from 5% to 25%, Techstrong.ai reported, citing Artificial Analysis. The model reached 86.3% on SWE-Bench Pro v2 (Hard), but scored only 13.1% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, MarkTechPost noted. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash still leads on several coding tests, according to The Decoder.

The better scores cost more to get. Artificial Analysis found the model produces about four times as many output tokens per task as its predecessor, which raised the average cost per task to $1.18 from $0.20, Techstrong.ai reported. That is still well below Gemini 3.8 Flash at $7.77 and Claude Sonnet 5.5 at $10.02, per The Decoder. The model supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens and was trained natively in Nvidia's NVFP4 four-bit format, i-SCOOP reported.

sections.heading: A staged path to open weights
sections.body:
The closed launch follows what the company calls its "safe path to open weights." Developers can already fine-tune and sample from the model on Tinker, and checkpoints will become downloadable once the weights are released, the lab said. The company's own product page is less specific. It says the weights will come "in the coming weeks," pending the results of more safety testing.

Thinking Machines also acknowledged some weaknesses. The model sometimes communicates inefficiently, does not always choose the best tools for large codebases, does not support audio, and is less optimized for chat, The Decoder reported. The release comes as the company is reportedly close to closing a $5 billion funding round, according to Techstrong.ai.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Cyber After AI Helps Find 81 Firefox Flaws, 948 Linux Exploits - The Hacker News
summary: OpenAI unveils GPT-6 Cyber, reporting 948 Linux privilege escalation exploits and 81 unknown Firefox flaws discovered with its help.
text:
OpenAI on Thursday unveiled GPT‑6 Cyber , which it described as a major step forward in security research that brings together stronger cybersecurity capabilities with a step-change improvement in model alignment.

The new model is "more capable at finding and fixing vulnerabilities, and far more reliable staying within the boundaries researchers set," OpenAI said . It has classified the model as Critical in cybersecurity under its Preparedness Framework.

The artificial intelligence (AI) company said GPT‑6 Cyber is also better than its predecessors like GPT‑5.6 Cyber and GPT‑6 Astra when it comes to following task boundaries and avoiding exploiting out-of-scope services in 99.93% of cases, up from 94.49% for GPT-5.6 Cyber.

It also scores 48.5% on ExploitGym, a cybersecurity benchmark that evaluates the capabilities of AI agents to autonomously turn known software vulnerabilities into functioning, real-world exploits. In comparison, GPT-5.6 Cyber scored 32.1%.

OpenAI said the model enabled the discovery of 948 local privilege escalation exploits in Linux⁠ through an autonomous pipeline, along with 81 previously unknown high-severity vulnerabilities in Mozilla Firefox and a critical vulnerability in Brotli⁠ (CVE-2026-111497, CVSS score: 9.2).

title: Google’s November Pixel update is missing, and Android 17 QPR2 may explain why - Android Authority
summary: The Android 17 QPR2 update could be just around the corner according to some theories being tossed around by Android users on Reddit. Google's QPR updates
text:
Android 17 QPR2 could be coming to Pixel devices early, according to suspicions from users on Reddit who have pointed out a few key details.

The Android 17 QPR2 update could be just around the corner according to some theories being tossed around by Android users on Reddit. Google’s QPR updates otherwise known as the quarterly updates that are sent out to the company’s Pixel devices, are sent out every few months. For instance, the last quarterly update was Android 17 QPR1 , and Google rolled that out to compatible Pixel devices back on September 15 alongside the latest Pixel drop at that time. Before that was stable Android 17 update in June, and before that was the quarterly update with a Pixel drop for Android 16 in March.

The next quarterly update, which will be Android 17 QPR2, would be expected to drop for Pixel owners sometime in December. This follows Google’s typical quarterly release schedule for these types of software updates. And in between, it pushes out the smaller security updates on a monthly basis. Sometimes these updates include a tweak or two to the features. But for the most part, they’re about stability and bug/security fixes. Some users think that Google is prepping an early drop of the new QPR update though.

title: Nvidia requires chip tracking for Southeast Asia partners
summary: Southeast Asian customers must join Nvidia's fleet intelligence system to become Nvidia Cloud Partners, Bloomberg reports, amid scrutiny over smuggling to China.
bullets:
- **Nvidia** NVIDIA Corporation now requires Southeast Asian customers to enroll in its **fleet intelligence** tracking system to earn Nvidia Cloud Partner status, according to Bloomberg.
- The NCP label offers priority access to Nvidia's most sought-after chips, giving cloud providers a strong reason to join the voluntary system.
- Authorities believe Chinese firms obtained billions in restricted chips through Southeast Asian smuggling networks, with Singapore-based **Megaspeed** under US and Singapore investigation.

sections.heading: Nvidia tightens chip tracking in Southeast Asia to fight smuggling
sections.body: Nvidia now requires customers in Southeast Asia to join its "fleet intelligence" chip-tracking system before they can become official Nvidia Cloud Partners (NCPs), Bloomberg reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter. The company has faced criticism that it hasn't done enough to keep its AI accelerators from reaching Chinese companies illegally. Bloomberg describes the new rule as a way to give Nvidia more visibility in a region that has long been used to reroute restricted goods.

sections.heading: Using partner status as an incentive
sections.body:
Fleet intelligence tracks where participating companies' AI accelerators are located, along with other metrics. It remains voluntary. Nvidia is using the NCP label to get more customers to sign up, according to Bloomberg. Cloud providers want the designation because it serves as a public endorsement and gives them priority access to chips.

Nvidia launched the tool nearly a year ago. It is mainly software for managing data centers, but because it records where individual parts are located, it also responds to US concerns about chips being diverted. By default, though, users don't have to share location data with Nvidia or the US government, Bloomberg reported. Nvidia declined to say whether existing partners will have to enroll to keep their status, or whether the requirement will apply outside Southeast Asia.

sections.heading: The Megaspeed case
sections.body:
US rules generally bar Chinese companies from buying advanced Nvidia AI chips without a license. Even so, authorities believe firms there have obtained billions of dollars' worth of the hardware, mostly through smuggling networks in Southeast Asia, Bloomberg reported.

Much of the scrutiny centers on Singapore-based Megaspeed International. The company has been under US and Singapore investigation for more than a year, and it won NCP status within a week of its founding in 2023. Last week, The New York Times reported that Washington suspects one of Megaspeed's top executives of spying for Beijing. Chief Executive Jensen Huang called his interactions with the company "completely normal" and said Nvidia had "counted every one" of the GPUs Megaspeed deployed. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing, and key House Republicans have asked Huang for a briefing, according to Bloomberg.

sections.heading: Wider crackdown
sections.body:
The tracking rule adds to other steps Nvidia has taken. Earlier this year, after the largest US chip-smuggling indictment, it removed half of the Asian firms it had pre-approved to buy chips. It has also told buyers not to rent more than half of their Nvidia computing power to Chinese companies, Bloomberg reported. The indictment came in March, when Super Micro Computer co-founder Wally Liaw was arrested on charges of plotting to smuggle $2.5 billion worth of Nvidia GPU servers into China, TipRanks noted.

Nvidia and parts of Washington still disagree over who should stop smuggling. Some officials say the company has repeatedly missed warning signs. Nvidia says it follows the law as written and that it is up to government officials to identify bad actors.

title: Apple's First Touchscreen Mac is Now Arriving to Customers - MacRumors
summary: It's Friday, November 6 in Australia and New Zealand, which means customers who preordered a PROLED touchscreen MacBook Pro, OLED iPad mini, M6 MacBook Pro, or M6 iMac are now starting to receive their devices.
text:
People will soon be sharing photos and first impressions of the new products on the MacRumors forums, Reddit, Instagram, and other platforms, giving us a first look at what real-world users think of the ‌OLED‌ upgrade for the ‌iPad mini‌ and the PROLED and touchscreen update for the ‌MacBook Pro‌.

Apple's new high-end ‌MacBook Pro‌ models come with M5 Pro or M5 Max, and the major change is the display. It's touch-enabled and is the first Mac with an ‌OLED‌ display. The design has been updated, so the new machines are thinner and lighter than the mini-LED models, which Apple is still selling. Apple also brought back the glowing Apple logo, and replaced the notch with a Dynamic Island . Pricing on the PROLED ‌MacBook Pro‌ starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch model and $3,399 for the 16-inch model.

The ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌ is Apple's first smaller-screened iPad to get ‌OLED‌, and it's also the most affordable ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad‌. It's almost a millimeter thinner than the prior version and has an Acoustic Display that does away with speaker holes. Without them, the enclosure is sealed, making it the first ‌iPad‌ with a water and dust resistance rating (IP67). It uses Apple's A20 Pro chip. The ‌OLED‌ ‌iPad mini‌ starts at $699.

The 14-inch entry-level ‌MacBook Pro‌ and 24-inch ‌iMac‌ got little in the way of updates beyond an M6 chip. The ‌MacBook Pro‌ is priced starting at $1,999, and the ‌iMac‌ starts at $1,499.
